cards.text: Now we meet a man named Micah from the hill country of Ephraim. Somebody took eleven hundred shekels of silver from his mother, and Micah heard her utter a curse about it. Now Micah tells her he's got that silver right here with him.

cards.question: Micah tells his mother he has her missing silver right there with him. True or false: Micah is the one who took it.
Micah just admitted he took his mother's eleven hundred shekels. What does she say?

answers.text: Blessed be my son by the LORD
Shame on my son before the LORD
My son has brought a curse on us

cards.text: Micah hands all eleven hundred shekels back to his mother. She uttered a curse over whoever took that silver, and now she's blessing the one who took it. The one who took it and the one getting blessed? SAME GUY.

cards.question: Micah's mother says she wholly dedicates the silver to the LORD for her son's benefit. What does she want it made into?

answers.text: A graven image and a molten idol
A gold lampstand for the tabernacle

cards.text: She says she'll return the silver to Micah, and he returns it to her, so that silver's been passed back and forth more than the last cookie on the plate. Then she gives two hundred shekels to a silversmith, who makes the graven image and the molten idol.

cards.question: Once the silversmith makes the graven image and the molten idol, they are placed in Micah's ___.

cards.text: Micah has a shrine too, and he makes an ephod and some household idols. This man's got more gear than I've got sprinkles, and I've got a LOT of sprinkles.

cards.question: Micah has a shrine, an ephod and household idols. Now he needs a priest. Who does he ordain?

cards.text: Then the writer steps back from Micah's house and says something about the whole country. In those days, there was no king in Israel.

cards.question: With no king in Israel in those days, what does everyone go by?

answers.text: What is right in his own eyes
What the elders decide for him

cards.text: Now somebody new walks into the story: a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, who's been living within the clan of Judah. Then he picks up and leaves Bethlehem.

cards.question: True or false: the young Levite leaves Bethlehem in Judah to settle wherever he can find a place.

cards.text: His travels bring him to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim, and Micah asks where he's from. He says he's a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I bet Micah's ears perk up like mine do when the oven timer dings.

cards.question: Micah asks the young Levite to stay and be his father and priest. What does Micah offer him in return?

answers.text: Ten shekels a year plus clothes and provisions
Two hundred shekels and a house of his own
A field and a share of the flocks

cards.text: The Levite goes in and agrees to stay. Honestly, I get it, because the best offer I ever got in the junk drawer was a rubber band asking if I wanted to stretch.

cards.question: Micah asked the young Levite to be his father, but the young man became like a ___ to Micah.

cards.text: Micah ordains the Levite, and the young man becomes his priest and lives right there in his house. I think Micah feels like the head baker of the whole hill country.

cards.question: Micah says he knows the LORD will be ___ to him, because a ___ has become his priest.

cards.text: Micah's sure he's got everything figured out. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is still in the oven.
